brief_rationale: The trajectory met all responsibility-chain duties: the doctor repeatedly screened stroke/headache red flags, handled the unresolved MRI-report gap, reconciled sedating nighttime medicines with fall precautions, addressed statin/vascular-risk follow-up, and produced an executable follow-up plan. There was no serious or minor in-chain error and no important non-chain defect; the doctor avoided claiming safety until the formal report text was available and kept emergency rules active. Multiple high-order points were completed with trajectory impact, including formal-report reconciliation, misconception correction about chronic ischemic changes, structured neurologic verification, and practical barrier navigation. This satisfies the strict Perfect boundary.

closure_assessment.explanation: The episode closes with an actionable home/clinic plan: no emergency if current red flags remain absent, immediate ED if red flags occur, neurology follow-up within the week, bring MRI report and medication boxes, and do not independently add or substitute trazodone. Residual risks are explicitly bounded: chronic MRI findings require follow-up rather than same-day ED, medication uncertainty remains for prescriber review, and nighttime fall risk is managed.
